purpose: Define evidence-based gates for making SEIS credible against enterprise-grade creative engineering platforms.
non_claims: This file does not claim SEIS already beats any large company product.
This file does not approve deployment, credentials, live provider routing, or customer production use.
This file defines gates that must be proven before strong market claims are made.

gates.title: Product clarity
gates.target: A reviewer can understand what SEIS is, who it serves, and what is runnable in under ten minutes.

gates.title: Architecture depth
gates.target: SEIS has visible architecture layers for product, AI, data, native platforms, validation, and governance.

gates.title: Trust and safety
gates.target: Secrets, provider keys, SSH, deployment, private data, and autonomous writes stay explicitly gated.

gates.title: Validation system
gates.target: Important claims are backed by scripts, manifests, review packets, or reproducible local checks.

gates.title: Developer experience
gates.target: A contributor can find the right route, run local checks, and understand rollback expectations without private context.

gates.title: Native platform depth
gates.target: Apple-first, systems, mobile, Windows, infrastructure, and data lanes have typed or declarative seed contracts.

gates.title: Market positioning
gates.target: SEIS has a credible moat story that explains why it is not just a dashboard, portfolio, code editor, or AI wrapper.
